chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Four [things] are not valid in four [contexts]: Treason, Ghulul (booty taken unlawfully), Theft, and Usury; they are not valid in Hajj, nor Umrah, nor Jihad, nor Charity.

key_terms.الْغُلُولُ: Booty or property taken unlawfully, especially by one party in a group

ai.seo_question: What are the four sources of wealth that invalidate acts of worship like Hajj and Charity in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing that wealth tainted by four specific defects—treason (*al-khiyanah*), war booty misappropriation (*al-ghulul*), theft (*al-sariqah*), and usury (*al-riba*)—is invalid for expiating religious duties. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the spiritual validity of acts of worship, such as Hajj, Umrah, Jihad, and Sadaqah, is contingent not only on ritual correctness but also on the purity of the source of funds used.
